metadata.title: Gaia DR3 in 6D: The search for fast hypervelocity stars and constraints on the Galactic Centre environment

evidence.quote: is the most promising HVS candidate
To identify possible HVS candidates unbound to the Galaxy consistent with coming from the Galactic Centre
These stars are shown as red circles in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2.

values.condition: total three-dimensional velocity in the Galactocentric rest frame; reported approximately as ∼600 km s−1

evidence.quote:
we cannot exclude the presence of HVSs in Gaia DR3 that are unbound and have radial velocities, but lack pre-
cise (or accurate) astrometry that can provide a robust determination
of the initial conditions for orbital integration. One such example is
Gaia DR3 4316462477768150144

values.condition: Gaia DR3 radial velocity, heliocentric/barycentric; rv_expected_sig_to_noise = 14

evidence.quote: Gaia DR3 4316462477768150144 with ν_rad = −804±7 km s−1 and rv_expected_sig_to_noise = 14

evidence.quote: The reported Gaia DR3 distance from the MARCS library is 2850+218−537 pc

notes: Gaia DR3 3126801097033888768 is retained as the paper's most promising HVS candidate (T:p5-b1); its Galactic Centre origin is described as poorly constrained, but the paper does not retract its unbound/HVS candidacy. Gaia DR3 4316462477768150144 is included as a conditional candidate: the paper says unbound HVSs lacking precise astrometry cannot be excluded and names this star as an example (T:p6-b9), although its parallax is highly uncertain and its nominal distance is said to be inconsistent with a GC origin. Gaia DR3 6023361538639059840 is not included because, although it is called the second HVS candidate, the authors explicitly conclude it is bound in all potential models (T:p5-b2). The 12-star Marchetti (2021) sample mentioned at T:p6-b10 is not individually identified in the supplied text and therefore could not be expanded into star entries.

Gaia DR3 3126801097033888768: In T:p5-b1, the target is reported with Galactocentric velocity components v_rGC = 591 ± 13 km/s and v_tanGC = 11_{-1}^{+4} km/s; these are not heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity or equatorial proper-motion components, so they are not extracted under those identifiers. The orbital quantity r_min = 505_{-156}^{+284} pc is a minimum disc-crossing radius rather than the present-day three-dimensional Galactocentric radius, so galactocentric_radius is not extracted. The distance error transcription has a negative sign on both the subscript and superscript sides; since both-negative asymmetric errors are logically inconsistent, the magnitudes 174 and 191 are recorded as lower and upper errors, respectively.

Gaia DR3 4316462477768150144: Target Gaia DR3 4316462477768150144 is discussed in Section 5 (p6-b9) as a star with a large negative radial velocity but imprecise astrometry (ruwe = 1.46, 6-parameter solution), so no orbital or Galactocentric quantities are reported for it. Its parallax (0.094 ± 0.12 mas) is highly uncertain and the paper states the MARCS distance (2850 pc) is inconsistent with a Galactic Centre origin. No right ascension or declination is given for this source in the paper.
